concepts.name: keycap-observatory
concepts.prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one realistic, production-quality Windows .NET MAUI desktop app UI concept for "AI Reset Radar", dark mode only, target dimensions 1440 x 1024. Reference image attached: Creator Micro editor, use its charcoal #1B1C20/#141519 canvas, graphite #222329 surfaces, restrained lavender #B5A0F4 and purple #7169CA accents, subtle #3B3D47 borders, Segoe UI typography, softly rounded controls, quiet dimensional depth. Translate its aesthetic into an AI quota monitor; do not copy the keypad literally unless asked by the direction. App title upper left with small radar brand mark, Refresh and Settings upper right. Intended user is an individual developer monitoring multiple provider accounts. Date anchor 2026-10-25 America/Chicago. All figures are illustrative demo data. Must make USED, LEFT, and RESET unambiguous for each window; no universal combined percent across providers. Example account OpenAI / Personal has Codex 5-hour: 38% used, 62% left, resets in 2h 14m; Codex weekly: 74% used, 26% left, resets Tue Oct 27 at 9:00 AM. GitHub Copilot / Work: AI credits 8,200 used of 10,000, 1,800 left, resets Oct 31 at 7 PM CDT (Nov 1 UTC). A second OpenAI / Work account can show 81% left, separate identity. Show "Updated just now" discreetly. No invented current plan prices or message counts. Main use case: quickly see which account has capacity and what resets next. Focused screen with readable 14-16px body, generous spacing, no card nesting or feature inventory. One primary action, one or two supporting areas, purposeful grouping and light dividers. Include a small tasteful dark popup at lower right "Codex weekly is running low · 26% left" with "View account" and "Snooze". Full app screen edge to edge, no computer hardware, no angled perspective, no marketing headline, no giant decorative radar taking space from information, no image montage, no external option numbering. Use exact product title. Direction-specific instructions follow: Direction name: "Keycap Observatory". The closest sibling to Creator Micro. Three large softly beveled account tiles across the central area, like premium charcoal keycaps, each with a provider glyph, account nickname, a large lavender remaining-capacity ring and an explicit LEFT value. Each relevant quota window gets a thin labeled used bar and reset countdown beneath. Selected OpenAI tile has lavender edge and a connected concise detail area below showing both 5-hour and weekly windows. Spacious, polished, tactile, calm. Keep at most three main account surfaces, no overstuffed dashboard.
